details:
Currently there is no way to test Quest worlds and Avatars before upload. This makes it difficult for Quest content creators to ascertain whether or not their content looks and behaves as desired, and to the level of performance desired.
Additionally, the Avatar performance ranking does not seem to be entirely accurate with how well an avatar actually performs on quest, instead being more a generalized determination of how far it exceeds quest limitations whilst still being uploadable.
By adding a "Developer Mode" to VRC, with the ability to "locally host" private worlds, and offering a locally hosted "Avatar Test" world, in which an avatar's performance can be accurately gauged and recorded, would allow not only for Quest worlds to be more fully fleshed out and functional on upload, but provide a more flexible rating system for Quest content, allowing for lax limitations on components of each in exchange for a minimum performance ranking to upload.
Some worlds poorly perform on Quest currently, as do some avatars, despite being "recommended" or falling within minimum "performance" guidelines. Whereas some "less performant" worlds and avatars cause no issue when viewed on Quest (or at the very least, Quest 2) systems. Without functional testing and performance metrics, it is not possible to truly ascertain a world's functional status.
One method this testing could be carried out is by creating a "test upload" function, which allows the content to be uploaded to an account without the ability to be accessed via other users. In the event of worlds, they would be accessible only by the content creator ("local only"/private no-invite), and the upload could be set to expire in X amount of days (say, a week?), removing it from their VRC account after that time.
Likewise, if a test avatar is submitted, a similar "local only" test world, made up of a blank black room with a solid floor, simple lighting, the avatar's pedestal, and button for a mirror, would appear. Entering this world could enable additional performance metrics collection, which, through a series of tests, would then be relayed to the SDK, and determine the performance of the avatar and whether it can be uploaded; as well this would allow the creator to ascertain whether the avatar functions as desired.
Testing could be limited to one world, and one avatar, per account, requiring them to "overwrite" an existing test world/avatar on upload of a different one, to conserve space.
In all, testing is a much needed feature if VRC on Quest is to continue, and whilst it is more difficult to test on the system without sideloading tactics, I feel that this method (which prevents others from accessing test content, and offers better performance rating of content), would greatly expand the availability of well performing Quest content, as well as give developers more freedom to create content with previously limited components, permitting they pass specific performance ratings.
title: [Quest]: On-device "Developer Mode" testing for "locally hosted" Avatars & Worlds
